To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression of melanoma antigen-A (MAGE) in regional lymph nodes (RLNs) is associated with a poor prognosis of patients with non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC).

(i) the presence of MAGE-A expression in tumor cells in lymph nodes was associated with a significantly shorter disease-free survival and overall survival; (ii) the presence of tumor cells with MAGE-A expression was associated with a higher risk of relapse and death, and (iii) the presence of disseminated tumor cells with MACE-A expression in regional lymph nodes was an independent prognostic factor.

(i) MAGE-A expression was detected in 10 of 20 (50%) patients with disseminated tumor cells (DTC) in the lymph nodes of patients undergoing resection of non-small cell lung carcinoma; and (ii) MAGE-A-positive DTC were associated with a significantly shorter disease-free survival (p = 0.02) than patients with MAGE-A-negative DTC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of MAGE-A in disseminated tumor cell in regional lymph nodes in patients with operable NSCLC.
the development of a novel approach for the detection of disseminated tumor cells (DTC) in regional lymph nodes.
the expression of the melanoma antigen A (MAGE-A), in the disseminated tumor cells of regional lymph nodes of non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC) patients.

the use of the MAGE-A gene family in the context of the MAGE-3 gene family is a promising approach to the development of the MAGE gene family in the treatment of lung cancer.
